before.rappel_count_note: Both counts are the same descent with a different rope setup. One published South Ridge description: "The rappel can be done in four raps with a 60M rope." The three stations listed here are the two-rope sequence — a double-rope rappel from the summit bolts to the ledge atop pitch 2, a short single to the top of pitch 1, then one more to the base. Do not rappel straight from the summit to the top of pitch 2 on one rope: it falls about 15 ft short and the crack below the anchor jams ropes.

before.turnaround: Set a turnaround time before starting and stick to it; the descent involves down-climbing loose, exposed terrain (including the summit chimney) that is markedly harder and slower in poor visibility, rain, or fading light.
before.detailed_rack: No rock rack is needed - this is an unroped Class 3 scramble. A helmet is recommended for the summit chimney and any loose rock below it, and many parties carry an ice axe and/or microspikes for lingering snow near Melakwa Pass early in the season.
